title: Cloudflare Adds Agent Tracing, with Truncation Limits and Uneven Payload Defaults
gist: Cloudflare shipped agent tracing as the first component of Cloudflare Agents, adding agent/model/tool/approval spans on top of existing Workers infrastructure tracing, free during beta and metered under Workers Observability pricing from October 1, 2026. The reporting flags three commercial and compliance traps: opposite payload-recording defaults between the Think and Flue harnesses, span-size truncation that disqualifies replay as an audit trail, and per-span billing that makes a verbose harness cost far more than the dashboard implies.

themes.theme: Agent runtime telemetry as a new layer

insights.claim: Cloudflare has launched agent tracing as the first shipped component of Cloudflare Agents, adding agent-level spans on top of its existing Workers tracing and surfacing deployed agent sessions in a single dashboard.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is building an agent platform stack, not just an edge runtime; observability is the wedge and later components will likely be monetized the same way.
insights.quote: Cloudflare has launched agent tracing, the first component of Cloudflare Agents, a dashboard surface that gathers deployed agent sessions in one place.

insights.claim: Application telemetry is structurally blind to agent failure because an agent can return HTTP 200 while picking the wrong tool, passing stale context to a subagent, or burning tokens in a retry loop — the API request and database query show up, the causing behavior does not.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Creates a genuine new observability SKU that incumbent APM coverage does not satisfy; watch whether Datadog/Grafana-class vendors or runtime owners like Cloudflare capture it.
insights.quote: An agent can return HTTP 200 and still fail.
insights.locator: The problem statement is the useful part

insights.claim: Cloudflare's trace model emits one trace per agent turn with a fixed hierarchy — invoke_agent containing chat (model) and execute_tool, which in turn nests tool_approval — and subagent work nests under the invoking operation so a delegated chain across model, tool, D1 and KV renders as one waterfall.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A reusable schema for agent observability; products that cannot express the parent/subagent waterfall across app and infra layers will look primitive by comparison.

insights.claim: Cloudflare requires three identity fields to link spans to its dashboard — agent name for the logical implementation, agent ID for the instance, and conversation ID — and explicitly warns against deriving the agent name from a request or user identifier because that multiplies distinct agents in the view.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Cardinality discipline is now a first-class design decision in agent deployments; misconfiguration degrades the product and, given per-span billing, the bill.
insights.locator: Three fields tie spans to the dashboard

insights.claim: The same Cloudflare tracing feature ships with opposite privacy defaults depending on harness: Think (and wrapAISDK()) store no message or tool payloads unless storeMessages and storeTools are set, while Flue stores messages, system instructions, tool definitions, arguments and results by default and requires content: false to stop.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A silent compliance landmine — enterprises may be recording PII or secrets purely as a function of which harness they picked; a plausible source of future incidents and audit findings.
insights.quote: The same platform feature therefore ships with opposite privacy defaults depending on which harness a team already chose, and message payloads routinely carry personal data or secrets.
insights.locator: Payload recording is where teams need to pay attention

insights.claim: Agent message payloads routinely carry personal data or secrets, which makes default-on payload capture in an agent tracing product a data-governance decision rather than a debugging convenience.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Expect regulated buyers to demand payload-redaction controls as a procurement gate for agent platforms.
insights.locator: Payload recording is where teams need to pay attention

themes.theme: Replay is a debugging aid, not an audit trail

insights.claim: Cloudflare states its agent traces are not a complete or lossless record of a conversation: payload data is subject to span size limits so long messages, reasoning, tool arguments and results may be truncated, and session replay does not display images.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Anyone planning to use agent replay for regulatory evidence or dispute resolution needs a separate, lossless logging path — an opening for dedicated agent-audit vendors.
insights.quote: Teams treating replay as an audit trail rather than a debugging aid will find it does not carry that weight.
insights.locator: The documented limitations deserve equal attention

insights.claim: Cloudflare's session replay reassembles recorded conversation data across turns — messages, reasoning, tool calls with arguments and results, subagent activity — but explicitly replays recorded data rather than re-executing the agent.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Distinguishes replay from true deterministic re-execution; the harder re-execution problem remains unsolved and is a candidate for the next product tier.
insights.locator: Alongside the trace view, session replay

insights.claim: Cloudflare's approval spans capture only lifecycle events within a single Worker invocation and therefore do not measure how long a human waits before responding across invocations, leaving human-in-the-loop latency unmeasured in an approval workflow.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The metric enterprises most want for agent approval workflows — human bottleneck time — is missing, so ROI cases for HITL automation cannot be built from this data yet.
insights.quote: Human-in-the-loop latency, arguably the most interesting number in an approval workflow, is not what the span records.
insights.locator: One caveat sits inside the approval span

insights.claim: Cloudflare agent tracing is free during beta and moves under Workers Observability pricing from October 1, 2026, meaning teams instrumenting now face a scheduled cost cliff.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A dated monetization event — watch Q4 2026 for whether verbose agent instrumentation materially lifts Cloudflare developer-platform revenue per customer.
insights.quote: tracing is free during beta, and from October 1, 2026 it falls under Workers Observability pricing

insights.claim: From October 1, 2026 Cloudflare's Workers Free tier covers 200,000 observability events per day with three-day retention while Workers Paid includes 20 million events per month with seven-day retention and charges $0.60 per additional million events.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Concrete unit economics for pricing agent observability against Datadog-style per-host or per-GB models; $0.60/M events is the benchmark to compare rivals against.
insights.locator: From October 1, Workers Free covers 200,000 events per day

insights.claim: The metered unit in Cloudflare's agent tracing is every span — including spans from SDK internals and other Worker-level operations the Agents dashboard never displays — so the bill scales with harness verbosity rather than with what the user sees.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hidden cost amplification: framework choice becomes a direct cost lever, and buyers should model span-per-turn counts before committing to a harness.
insights.quote: A verbose harness costs more than the dashboard suggests, and three to seven days is short for anyone chasing a pattern rather than an incident.
insights.locator: The pricing detail rewards a close read

insights.claim: Three-to-seven-day trace retention is too short for diagnosing behavioral patterns in agents as opposed to point-in-time incidents, implying teams will need to export traces to longer-lived stores.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Creates pull-through demand for third-party OTLP-compatible backends; retention limits, not ingestion, are where competing vendors can win the account.
insights.locator: The pricing detail rewards a close read

insights.claim: Cloudflare Workers does not yet support the OpenTelemetry API directly, forcing custom agent harnesses onto a Workers custom spans API modeled on OpenTelemetry's GenAI reference implementations, though Cloudflare says it is working to add direct support.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Manual instrumentation is a real adoption tax today; direct OTel API support would remove friction and is a concrete milestone to watch for Workers agent adoption.
insights.locator: Custom harnesses use the Workers custom spans API

insights.claim: Cloudflare's span attributes follow the OpenTelemetry Generative AI semantic conventions and traces export to any OTLP endpoint, keeping the data portable off Cloudflare's own dashboard.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Low switching cost on the data layer means Cloudflare must win on price and integration, not lock-in — good for buyers, margin pressure for the vendor.
insights.locator: Span attributes follow the OpenTelemetry Generative AI semantic conventions

insights.claim: Instrumentation effort in Cloudflare's model varies sharply by stack: Think and Flue v2+ instrument turns automatically, direct AI SDK calls need a wrapAISDK() wrapper supporting v6 and v7 with identity fields passed on every call, and custom harnesses require manual spans.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Framework choice determines observability cost of ownership; auto-instrumented harnesses gain a distribution advantage on the platform.

insights.claim: Multiple vendors converged on agent-runtime telemetry in the same quarter — Microsoft's Agent Framework harness shipped with OpenTelemetry enabled by default, and the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management exports token metrics to Application Insights, Datadog and Grafana — indicating the agent runtime now needs its own telemetry layer that infrastructure spans cannot supply.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A category is forming simultaneously across hyperscalers and edge providers — a signal to watch observability incumbents (Datadog, Grafana) for either capture or displacement.
insights.quote: Each reaches the same conclusion from a different direction: the agent runtime needs its own telemetry layer, and infrastructure spans alone cannot explain what an agent did.
insights.locator: The release fits a pattern visible across vendors this quarter

insights.claim: Cloudflare frames tracing as a step toward self-improving agents by feeding structured trace data into evaluations and an agent development lifecycle, but that remains only a stated direction with no shipped capability today.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Discount the self-improvement narrative in valuation; what actually shipped is model, token, tool and latency visibility for a single turn.
insights.quote: What exists today is visibility into which model a turn called, how many tokens it used, which tool it selected, and where the time went.
insights.locator: Cloudflare frames tracing as a step toward agents that improve themselves

insights.claim: Developer enthusiasm for the release centered on the adjacency of model calls and tool arguments in a single waterfall view rather than on any new capability, with one developer responding on X that seeing the model call directly above a bad tool argument is the debugging view they want.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Product-market fit here is about UI adjacency, not data collection — a low-moat differentiator that competitors can copy quickly.
insights.quote: I'd try this on hermes just for the trace waterfall - seeing the model call directly above a bad tool argument is the debugging view I want
insights.locator: That adjacency is what developers responded to
